title: How AI Is Revolutionizing Weather Forecasting

slides.heading: How AI Is Revolutionizing Weather Forecasting
slides.body: From 10-day forecasts to hurricane paths — machine learning is rewriting what's possible

slides.heading: The Old Way: Physics-Based Models
slides.body: Traditional weather forecasts run equations that simulate Earth's atmosphere at thousands of grid points. These numerical weather prediction (NWP) models require massive supercomputers and take hours to generate a single forecast.

slides.heading: AI Enters the Forecast Room
slides.body: Models like Google's GraphCast and Huawei's Pangu-Weather learn directly from 40+ years of historical weather data. Instead of solving physics equations, they learn patterns — and do it in minutes, not hours.

slides.heading: GraphCast: A 10-Day Forecast in 60 Seconds
slides.body: DeepMind's GraphCast outperformed the world's best traditional model (ECMWF) on 90% of test metrics. It runs on a single Google TPU and delivers a 10-day global forecast roughly 1,000x faster than conventional methods.

slides.heading: Better Hurricane Track Predictions
slides.body: AI models have shown measurably better accuracy at predicting tropical storm tracks 3–7 days out. More precise paths give coastal communities longer, better-targeted evacuation windows — a direct life-saving advantage.

slides.heading: Hyperlocal Forecasting
slides.body: Traditional models struggle below roughly 10 km resolution. AI downscaling can generate street-level predictions from coarse global data, enabling city-by-city flash flood alerts and minute-by-minute precipitation maps.

slides.heading: Extreme Weather in a Warming World
slides.body: Climate change is producing weather outside the range of historical training data — a known weakness for AI models. Researchers are blending physics constraints into neural networks to keep predictions reliable even in novel conditions.

slides.heading: The Democratization of Forecasting
slides.body: Because AI models run on a single GPU instead of a room full of supercomputers, smaller nations and research groups can now produce world-class forecasts. The barrier to high-quality weather prediction has collapsed.

slides.heading: Humans Still in the Loop
slides.body: Operational meteorologists verify AI output, catch edge cases, and communicate risk to the public. The best forecasting systems today combine AI speed with human expertise — neither alone beats the two working together.

slides.heading: The Future of Forecasting
slides.body: AI won't replace meteorology — it will supercharge it. Faster, cheaper, and more accurate predictions mean better-prepared communities, smarter energy grids, and lives saved when every hour of warning counts.
